purpose: One place that says whether two years of a measure can be compared. The dashboard's comparability indicators, the suppressed change figures, the colour-scale segments and the continuity columns in downloads all read this file. Having a value for every year does not make a valid trend: a change can come from how the data was collected, defined or mapped rather than from what happened.

availability.reason: The selected 2011-2013 source tables supply no comparable Special and Local Laws or crimes-against-women aggregates, so they are left blank, not zero.
The 2016 extract supplies theft and robbery only. Its burglary figure combines criminal trespass and burglary, and its other aggregates use incompatible source definitions, so they are left blank.

definitionBreaks.reason: NCRB changed its reporting format and offence groupings in 2014, after the 2013 criminal-law changes. 2014 counts are not on the same basis as 2013, and the old burglary head and the revised criminal-trespass/burglary head are different measures.
2016 comes from a different compilation (the India Data Portal extract of NCRB data) than the 2011-2015 NCRB tables.
Burglary up to 2015 is the revised criminal-trespass/burglary head; from 2017 it is the day-plus-night burglary definition.

Up to 2015 the figure is the total printed in the original-year table; from 2016 it is the IPC plus SLL total of the State/UT tables. Crime in India 2017 prints 17,222 for 2015 where the original-year table gives 17,104, so the two heads are not identical.
NCRB prints 2,637 Delhi burglary cases for 2021 and 6,189 for 2022 (2.3 times as many) under the same heading. The cause has not been established, so read the change with caution.
2016-2021 come from the India Data Portal extract and 2022 onward from NCRB's own district-wise tables.

Up to 2015 the Delhi-wide figures come from the original-year summary tables; from 2016 they are the Delhi row of Table 1A.4 of each year's Crime in India edition. The printed section ranges differ between editions (2016 prints theft as Sec 379 to 382, robbery as Sec 392 to 394, and a combined criminal-trespass-and-burglary head as Sec 453 to 457).
The 2016 table prints theft as Sec 379 to 382 IPC and robbery as Sec 392 to 394 IPC; from 2017 they are Sec 379 IPC and Sec 392/394/397 IPC, so the two years may not count exactly the same offences.

Burglary (Sec 454 to 460 r/w 380 IPC) falls from 9,828 in 2017 to 4,147 in 2018 under the same printed heading, and no explanation was found in the reviewed NCRB material. Treat the fall as unexplained, not as a measured change in burglary.

The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the Indian Penal Code on 1 July 2024, so the 2024 tables use BNS numbering and offence groupings follow the source table. The hurt head is named "Hurt" in the 2023 table and "Hurt or Grievous Hurt" in the 2024 table, so it is not like-for-like. Press reports give a national fall in hurt cases of 30.58% and attribute it to the change, but the mechanism is not confirmed (simple hurt was already non-cognisable under IPC section 323). In Delhi the hurt head fell from 6,045 to 2,028, about 8% of the Delhi-wide fall; theft accounts for most of it (data/derived/bns_hurt_2023_2024.json).

epochs.reason: The same 11 district names are used, but no station-by-station roster exists for these years (the December 2014 roster is the only dated one), so a station moving between districts cannot be ruled out.

breaks.reason: Delhi Police districts were reorganised. Rohini and Shahdara were notified on 14 October 2016 and reported as newly created in early December 2016, and Dwarka followed on 9 November 2017. 48 of the 161 stations with archived shapes sit in a different district in the November 2017 schedule than in the December 2014 roster.
breaks.unaffectedNote: These four have the same station list in the December 2014 roster and the November 2017 schedule.

breaks.reason: Outer North was created on 1 January 2019 from parts of Rohini, North-West and Outer.
breaks.othersReason: Other station reassignments around 2019 are not documented.

utSeries.gapReason: No Delhi-wide figure has been collected for this year, so it is left blank rather than computed from districts.
utSeries.note: Delhi-wide totals do not depend on district boundaries, so geography breaks are skipped. Definition breaks and missing years still apply.

roadDistrict.reason2022: The 2022 road-death and hit-and-run figures use the Traffic Police's 11 reporting districts, not the 15 police districts, so they cannot be compared with 2023 or 2024.
roadDistrict.zoneReason2022: The 2022 report prints 15 Traffic Police districts under the same names as the police districts, but boundary identity has not been verified, and its crash-prone zones differ from those of 2023. Compare 2022 with 2023 with caution.
roadDistrict.cautionReason: These counts cover only each year's identified crash-prone zones, and the zone lists come from separate annual reports and list different zones; a change in a count is not a change in risk.

breaks.reason: Dwarka appears as a separate Traffic Police reporting row from 2018 (11 districts before, 12 after). District counts across this break are not compared, and no crosswalk to the earlier districts is documented.
The Traffic Police district tables go from 12 reporting units in 2021 to 15 in 2022. District counts across this break are not compared, and no crosswalk is documented.
The 2022 and 2023 tables both print 15 districts under the same names, but boundary continuity has not been verified.

roadHistory.sameSetReason: The same set of printed districts as the year before, but exact annual boundaries are not verified.
roadHistory.zoneReason: These are crashes within the zones identified that year, not all crashes in the district or on the road. The selected locations can change each year, so a change is not a change in risk at fixed places.
roadHistory.pandemicReason: 2020 and 2021 were affected by pandemic restrictions, which changes how raw counts should be read.

reasons: Counts, not rates: traffic and population changed over the period.
Injury and simple/non-injury figures differ by source edition and are excluded.
The early reports' standardized 30-day fatality definition could not be confirmed.

modeOfTravel.reason: The 2011 to 2018 figures use the older annual reports' own categories (for example "scooter and motorcycle riders"); the 2019 to 2024 series comes from the later reports with its own labels. The meaning is close but not identical.

reasons: The 2023 and 2024 lists come from separate reports and list different zones; a change in the number of zones is not a change in risk.
Year-to-date series (for example iRAD 2026) cover part of a year and are never compared with full years.
